values: Determines whether a healthcare service, treatment, device, test, or type of care is covered under the member’s applicable plan. This captures the very large population of terse service queries such as “MRI,” “urgent care,” “physical therapy,” or “breast pump,” as well as explicit coverage questions.

• Is physical therapy covered under this plan?
• What are my benefits for an MRI?
• Is a breast pump covered?
• What benefit applies to outpatient surgery?
• Does the member have caregiver benefits?

Member/plan: active plan, benefit package, effective dates
Benefit configuration: covered service/category, benefit definition, inclusion/exclusion rules
Service classification: service type, place of service, preventive vs. diagnostic, inpatient/outpatient
Conditions: age/gender/diagnosis requirements where applicable

Determines what the member is expected to pay for a covered service, including copay, coinsurance, deductible applicability, and other cost-sharing rules. “How much,” “copay,” and “cost” questions form a major recurring intent in the dataset.

• What is my copay for an MRI?
• How much will I pay for urgent care?
• What is the member cost for a colonoscopy?
• Is this service subject to coinsurance?
• What would I pay for outpatient surgery?

Benefit cost share: copay, coinsurance %, deductible applicability
Network tier: in-network/out-of-network cost share
Place of service: office, hospital, ambulatory center, ER, etc.
Benefit sequencing: before/after deductible rules
Member plan configuration: individual/family tier and applicable benefit

Determines whether a provider/facility is participating, which network tier applies, and how benefits change based on provider or place of service. Includes PCP/specialist questions and scenarios involving in-network facilities with out-of-network clinicians.

• Is this specialist in network?
• What benefit applies when the hospital is in network but the anesthesiologist is out of network?
• Can I see an out-of-network provider?
• Where can I find an in-network physical therapist?
• What is my benefit for a specialist office visit?

Provider directory: NPI/provider ID, specialty, facility, location
Network participation: network/product, effective/termination dates
Provider hierarchy: professional vs. facility provider
Place of serviceNetwork-specific benefits: INN/OON cost sharing, non-network restrictions, network exceptions

Answers questions specific to prescription drugs, formulary placement, pharmacy tiers, retail/mail/specialty pharmacy, and drug-specific coverage. This warrants its own taxonomy because the source data is substantially different from medical benefits.

• What is my copay for prescription drugs?
• What is the benefit for a Tier 3 medication?
• Is Zepbound covered?
• Which specialty pharmacy should I use?
• Is this medication on the formulary?

Formulary: drug/NDC/RxNorm identifier, formulary status
Drug tier: Tier 1–n / preferred/non-preferred/specialty
Pharmacy benefit: retail, mail order, specialty; days supply
Cost share: copay/coinsurance, Rx deductible
Utilization management: PA, step therapy, quantity limits
Pharmacy network: participating/specialty pharmacy

Maps a CPT, HCPCS, ICD, revenue, or other billing code to the appropriate benefit/service category before coverage can be determined. Thousands of entries consist primarily of a code such as 99214, 99213, or a question about which benefit a CPT belongs to.

• What benefit does CPT 78013 fall under?
• What are the benefits for CPT 99214?
• Is CPT 77067 covered?
• Which benefit category applies to this procedure code?
• What is the member cost for CPT 45378?

Code sets: CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, revenue codes
Code descriptions and hierarchies
Code-to-benefit mapping
Code-to-service category mapping
Place-of-service compatibility
Plan benefit configuration
Potentially diagnosis/procedure pairing when coverage is conditional

Determines how coverage works when the member receives care outside the plan’s normal service area, outside California, in another state, or internationally. This is a distinct and recurring pattern in the questions.

• If I’m traveling outside California, do I have coverage?
• What are my out-of-state benefits?
• Can I use a BlueCard provider in another state?
• Is emergency care covered while traveling?
• Do I have international travel coverage?

Plan service area / geography
Member home region
National/network reciprocity: e.g., BlueCard/network partner rules
Travel benefit rules
Emergency vs. routine care distinctions
International coverage rules
**Out-of-area network status and cost share
Determines whether a service requires prior authorization, precertification, referral, medical-necessity review, or another prerequisite before the service is received.

• Does an MRI require prior authorization?
• Do I need a referral to see a specialist?
• Does a CT scan require preauthorization?
• Can the member self-refer for mental health services?
• What authorization is required for this medication/procedure?

Utilization-management rules
Service/CPT authorization requirements
Referral requirements by plan/productProvider/specialty rules
Medical policy / clinical criteria references
Prior-auth vendor/process information
Effective dates and exceptions
Answers questions about the plan deductible and out-of-pocket maximum, including what applies to them and—where transaction/member data is available—how much has been met or remains.

• What is my deductible?
• How much of my deductible have I met?
• What is my out-of-pocket maximum?
• Does emergency care apply toward the deductible?
• How do the individual and family deductibles work together?

Plan accumulator configuration: deductible/OOP limits
Individual vs. family accumulators
Current accumulated amounts
Remaining balancesINN/OON accumulator separation
Benefit-to-accumulator rules
Benefit/calendar year dates
Determines quantitative restrictions on an otherwise covered benefit—number of visits, units, pairs, sessions, days, age limits, replacement intervals, or annual/lifetime maximums.

• How many physical therapy visits are covered?
• Is there an annual limit on chiropractic visits?
• How often can I receive this preventive service?
• Is there an age limit for this benefit?
• How many pairs of orthotics are covered?

Benefit limits: visits, units, days, dollar maximums
Frequency rules: per year, rolling period, lifetime, replacement interval
Age/gender restrictions
Benefit-period definition
Accumulated utilization, if determining remaining benefit
Exception/medical-necessity rules

Captures the smaller but distinct operational question set involving EOBs, claims, reimbursement, member eligibility, dependent coverage, and plan enrollment context. These questions require transaction/member data beyond static benefit configuration.

• Why does my EOB show a copay but no patient responsibility?
• Can I submit a superbill for out-of-network reimbursement?
• Is this dependent currently covered?
• When did the member’s coverage become effective?
• Why was this claim denied?

Member eligibility: coverage dates, subscriber/dependent relationships, product
Claim header/lines: service date, provider, codes, billed/allowed amounts
Adjudication: status, denial/remark codes, adjustments
EOB/member responsibility
Payment/reimbursement data
Appeal/reimbursement rules

values:
Get help with COBRA or account-specific coverage changes: Help a member understand where to address COBRA or other account-specific plan administration changes that are not supported directly in chat. 

Illustrative question: “Who can help me with a change to my COBRA coverage?”

Given the member is authenticated and the requested account change is not supported as a chat transaction When the member asks for help with COBRA or another account-specific coverage change Then Compass Member Chat should provide the available account information, explain the supported next step, and route the member to the appropriate servicing channel when required
Eligibility - coverage type Member account - servicing guidance
Avoid dead-end responses; identify the correct servicing path and what the member should have ready.

Update member contact information: Help a member change supported account details such as an email address through an authenticated account-management workflow. 

Illustrative question: “Can I update the email address on my account?”

Given the member is authenticated and the requested profile field is eligible for self-service update When the member asks to update supported contact information Then Compass Member Chat should collect the new value, confirm the change, and update the authoritative account through the supported workflow
Member demographics - email Member account - profile
Require explicit confirmation before changing account data and reflect successful versus failed updates clearly.

Understand individual versus family accumulators: Help a member understand how individual and family deductibles or out-of-pocket maximums relate and which balances apply to them. 

Illustrative question: “Why do I have an individual deductible and a family deductible?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable accumulator definitions are available When the member asks how individual and family accumulators work together Then Compass Member Chat should explain the applicable individual and family accumulator rules and relate them to the member’s available balances
Accumulators - individual balances Accumulators - family balances Plan benefits - accumulator rules
Explain embedded versus aggregate concepts only when supported by plan data; use examples without implying future claim outcomes.

Schedule a healthcare appointment: Help a member find an appropriate scheduling path and, when the supported integration is available, book an appointment with a selected provider or location. 

Illustrative question: “Can you schedule an appointment with an in-network primary care doctor?”

Given the member is authenticated and an in-scope scheduling integration is available When the member asks to schedule an appointment Then Compass Member Chat should guide provider/time selection, obtain confirmation, and complete the supported booking or route the member to the appropriate scheduling path
Provider directory Scheduling - appointment availability Scheduling - booking details
Roadmap scope remains discovery-dependent; distinguish search/navigation from a confirmed booking transaction.

Understand benefit limits or restrictions: Help a member understand visit limits, frequency limits, exclusions, prerequisites, or other restrictions that affect use of a covered benefit. 

Illustrative question: “How many physical therapy visits does my plan cover each year?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable benefit limitation data is available When the member asks about limits or restrictions on a benefit Then Compass Member Chat should explain the applicable limits, restrictions, and related disclosure language available in the plan data
Plan benefits - service level limitations Plan benefits - disclosure
State whether limits are annual, benefit-period, or service-specific when that context is available.

Check a premium or member bill due status: Help a member understand whether a supported bill is due and view available due-date or balance information. 

Illustrative question: “Do I have a payment due this month?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable billing data is available When the member asks whether a bill or payment is due Then Compass Member Chat should provide the available balance, due date, and relevant billing status information
Billing - balance Billing - due date Billing - status
Clearly identify which bill/account is being referenced and separate premium/member billing from provider bills.

Understand a general billing or payment question: Help a member understand supported billing rules, payment guidance, or account-level billing information without requiring a payment transaction. 

Illustrative question: “Why is my plan payment amount different this month?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable billing information is available When the member asks a general account-level billing or payment question Then Compass Member Chat should explain the available billing information and supported next steps, escalating when the issue requires account-specific case handling
Billing - account details Billing - payment guidance
Distinguish plan/account billing from medical claim/provider billing early in the conversation.

Make a supported payment: Help a member complete a payment through the planned billing workflow when the relevant payment capability is enabled. 

Illustrative question: “Can I pay my plan bill here?”

Given the member is authenticated, an eligible balance exists, and the payment transaction is available When the member asks to make a payment Then Compass Member Chat should present the payment details, obtain explicit confirmation, complete the supported transaction, and return a clear result
Billing - balance Payment - method/token Payment - transaction result
Use explicit confirmation and clear success/failure states; do not expose sensitive payment data in conversation history.

Manage autopay or recurring payment settings: Help a member enroll in, change, or understand supported automatic payment settings when that account capability is enabled. 

Illustrative question: “How do I turn on autopay?”

Given the member is authenticated and recurring-payment management is available When the member asks to enroll in or change autopay Then Compass Member Chat should explain the current setting, collect supported choices, obtain confirmation, and complete or route the recurring-payment change
Billing - autopay status Payment - recurring settings
Confirm effective timing and consequences before changing recurring payment settings.

Get guidance about renewal-related billing actions: Help a member understand supported renewal or payment actions associated with continued coverage when that billing scope is enabled. 

Illustrative question: “Do I need to do anything to renew or keep my coverage active?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable renewal/billing guidance is available When the member asks about renewal-related payment or billing requirements Then Compass Member Chat should explain the supported renewal or payment steps and direct the member to the correct action path
Billing - renewal status Billing - payment requirements Eligibility - coverage status
Avoid conflating plan renewal with eligibility enrollment rules when the required data is not available.

Resolve an unexpected bill or claim-payment discrepancy: Help a member understand whether an unexpected bill relates to claim processing, benefit cost-sharing, network status, or another issue and direct unresolved disputes appropriately. 

Illustrative question: “Why did I get this bill when I thought the service was covered?”

Given the member is authenticated and relevant claim and benefit information is available When the member asks about an unexpected provider bill or a payment discrepancy Then Compass Member Chat should explain the information available from benefits and claims, identify what cannot be determined from those sources, and escalate when a billing or claim dispute requires case review
Claims - Medical Claims - member responsibility Plan benefits - cost sharing rules Provider network context
Use progressive clarification before escalation; do not treat a provider bill as equivalent to an EOB or claim record.

Determine whether a referral is needed: Help a member understand whether plan rules require a referral before seeing a specialist or receiving a service. 

Illustrative question: “Do I need a referral to see a dermatologist?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable referral rules are available When the member asks whether a referral is required Then Compass Member Chat should explain the applicable referral requirement and supported next steps
Plan benefits - referral rules Plan benefits - service access requirements
Do not infer a referral requirement solely from provider type when plan-specific rules are unavailable.

Assess symptoms and navigate to an appropriate level of care: Help a member use the planned symptom-checking experience to answer symptom questions and receive an appropriate care-level recommendation and provider navigation. 

Illustrative question: “I have a bad sore throat and fever. What kind of care should I get?”

Given the member chooses to use symptom checking and the approved symptom-checker integration is available When the member describes symptoms and completes the guided questions Then Compass Member Chat should present the approved symptom-checker recommendation and supported care-navigation options within defined clinical handoff boundaries
Symptom checker - responses Care recommendation Provider navigation
Clinical governance and safety boundaries are required; do not substitute general generative responses for the approved symptom-checker result.

Get help appealing a denied claim: Help a member understand how to appeal a denied claim or obtain assistance when an appeal submission or dispute cannot be completed in chat. 

Illustrative question: “How do I appeal this denied claim?”

Given the member has a denied claim or claim dispute and available appeal guidance is known When the member asks how to appeal or reports a problem submitting an appeal Then Compass Member Chat should provide the supported appeal steps and route the member to the appropriate support channel when the appeal requires case handling or cannot be completed in chat
Claims - denial/rejection reason Appeals - process guidance
Claims and appeal disputes are a high-escalation area; make the handoff criteria and next steps explicit.

Understand why a claim was denied or rejected: Help a member understand the available denial or rejection reason and the next steps indicated by claim or EOB information. 

Illustrative question: “Why was my claim denied?”

Given the member is authenticated and claim denial or rejection details are available When the member asks why a claim was denied or rejected Then Compass Member Chat should explain the available reason in plain language and provide supported next-step guidance or escalation when resolution requires case review
Claims - status Claims - denial/rejection reason Claims - EOB messages
Distinguish an explanation of the recorded reason from adjudication advice; escalate disputes requiring human case review.

Check claim status: Help a member determine whether a submitted medical claim is received, pending, processed, denied, or otherwise in a known status. 

Illustrative question: “What is the status of my claim from last month?”

Given the member is authenticated and claim status data is available When the member asks for the status of a specific claim Then Compass Member Chat should identify the relevant claim and provide its current status and available status details
Support claim disambiguation by date/provider/service and show status in plain language.

Review claim details and member responsibility: Help a member understand available claim details, including billed amount, allowed amount, plan payment, and member responsibility. 

Illustrative question: “How much did my plan pay on this claim and what do I owe?”

Given the member is authenticated and claim detail data is available When the member asks about the financial details of a specific claim Then Compass Member Chat should summarize the available claim amounts and member responsibility and distinguish them from benefit estimates
Claims - Medical Claims - billed amount Claims - allowed amount Claims - plan paid Claims - member responsibility
Present a clear amount breakdown and avoid interpreting provider billing that is not represented in claim data.

Determine whether a healthcare service is covered: Help a member understand whether a medical service or procedure is covered under the applicable plan and surface relevant coverage conditions.

Illustrative question: “Is physical therapy covered under my plan?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable plan benefit data is available When the member asks whether a healthcare service is covered Then Compass Member Chat should explain the available plan-specific coverage and relevant benefit conditions
Plan benefits - covered services Plan benefits - disclosure
Surface plan-specific limitations and disclosure language; avoid implying coverage beyond available benefit data.

Check remaining deductible: Help a member see current deductible progress and how much remains before the applicable deductible is met. 

Illustrative question: “How much of my deductible do I have left?”

Given the member is authenticated and current accumulator data is available When the member asks how much deductible remains Then Compass Member Chat should provide the applicable deductible amount, amount accumulated, and remaining balance using the available member data
Accumulators - In Network Deductible Accumulators - Out Network Deductible
Identify the applicable network tier and data-as-of context when available.

Understand dental benefit coverage and limits: Help a member understand coverage, cost-sharing, and routine limits for dental services such as cleanings, crowns, or orthodontia. 

Illustrative question: “Does my dental plan cover a crown?”

Given the member is authenticated and applicable dental benefit data is available When the member asks about coverage or limits for a dental service Then Compass Member Chat should explain the available dental coverage, cost-sharing, and routine limits
Plan benefits - dental covered services Plan benefits - dental cost sharing Plan benefits - dental limits
Keep dental benefit explanations separate from dental claim-processing disputes.

Manage dependent information: Help a member understand or perform supported actions related to dependents on the account, while distinguishing informational access from enrollment changes that require another process. 

Illustrative question: “How do I add or update a dependent on my account?”

Given the member is authenticated and dependent/account information is available When the member asks about a dependent or a supported dependent-management action Then Compass Member Chat should provide available dependent information and complete or route the requested action according to supported account rules
Member account - dependents Eligibility - dependent coverage
Clarify whether the request is an account-profile change, eligibility/enrollment change, or informational question before acting.

Confirm current plan eligibility: Help a member confirm whether they are currently eligible for coverage under the applicable plan. 

Illustrative question: “Am I currently active on my health plan?”

Given the member is authenticated and authoritative eligibility data is available When the member asks whether their coverage is currently active Then Compass Member Chat should provide the available eligibility status and relevant plan context
Use authoritative member data and clearly identify the plan or coverage segment being referenced.

Understand coverage effective or termination dates: Help a member understand when coverage begins, ends, or changes based on available eligibility information. 

Illustrative question: “When does my coverage start?”

Given the member is authenticated and eligibility date information is available When the member asks when coverage begins or ends Then Compass Member Chat should provide the available effective or termination dates and related eligibility context
Eligibility - effective date Eligibility - termination date Eligibility - plan/product
Use date-specific language and avoid explaining enrollment policy beyond the eligibility data available.

Get human support when the issue cannot be resolved in chat: Help a member reach the appropriate support channel when the request requires case management, a transaction outside chat scope, or information the agent cannot reliably resolve. Illustrative question: “Can someone help me with this claim issue?”

Given the member has an unresolved request that is outside supported chat resolution or requires human case review When the member asks for human help or the agent determines a handoff is appropriate Then Compass Member Chat should explain why additional support is needed, provide or initiate the supported handoff path, and communicate relevant callback or availability expectations
Conversation context Escalation reason Callback/contact details
Attempt reasonable clarification before offering a callback; set expectations about callback timing and preserve context for the handoff.

Understand an Explanation of Benefits: Help a member interpret the key information on an EOB, including claim processing, plan payment, member responsibility, and explanatory messages. Illustrative question: “Can you explain what this EOB means?”

Given the member is authenticated and EOB data is available When the member asks for help understanding an EOB Then Compass Member Chat should explain the available EOB fields and messages in plain language and identify any next step stated in the EOB data
Claims - EOB Claims - adjustment/reason messages Claims - member responsibility
Explain that an EOB is not itself a provider bill and preserve official reason-message meaning.

Use Member Chat in a supported preferred language: Help a member conduct the conversational experience in a supported language while preserving accurate benefit terminology, required disclosures, and navigation. Illustrative question: “Can I continue this chat in Spanish?”
